text:
alex: Quick heads-up — saw a perf regression on MI250 int8 inference path. Traces show routing fell back to generic_gemm_v2 for seqlen=128 batch=4 -> p50 latency +120ms (~2.1x). Suspect missing registered kernel: int8_mi250_tile_64.
priya: logs?
alex: pasted snippet from node logs: "kernel_lookup: candidate not found: int8_mi250_tile_64" then "route=soft_fallback generic_gemm_v2". Happened intermittently during canary.
ci-bot: perf-ci job #745: int8 throughput down 42% on rocm-mi250 after last runtime change. baseline 2100 tok/s -> 1220 tok/s on HEAD.
morgan: did KV-cache patterns change? fallback could disable some KV fastpaths and blow latency.
alex: KV metrics show prefix_kv_hit_rate stable (~0.86) but cache_miss spikes line up with fallback events. So not a KV correctness issue, it's the kernel selection.
priya: autonunner/autotune registry — maybe the tile was filtered out by arch rules.
alex: correct — autotune registry has an entry but it's excluded for gfx90a due to a past correctness hit. That exclusion explains lookup miss.
morgan: we should update routing to prefer arch+dtype exact matches. If none, allow a controlled soft_fallback with a scoring penalty threshold (so we know when it degrades). Add telemetry for soft_fallback_count and penalty magnitude.
priya: also consider seqlen-aware picks: for seq <= 64 prefer int8_tile_32, for 65-256 prefer int8_tile_64. Current autotune picks a single winner per model, we should make it multi-bucketed.
alex: quick pseudo change for routing (for discussion):
```py
# runtime/routing.py
candidates = registry.lookup(key)
# prefer same-arch and same-dtype, then stability/score
candidates.sort(key=lambda c: (c.arch == host_arch, c.dtype == req.dtype, c.score, -c.stability), reverse=True)
# allow fallback only if penalty acceptable
if candidates and candidates[0].arch != host_arch:
    if candidates[0].latency / (candidates[1].latency if len(candidates) > 1 else candidates[0].latency) > FALLBACK_THRESH:
        route = candidates[1]
    else:
        route = candidates[0]
else:
    route = candidates[0] if candidates else default_kernel
```
priya: minor: need to guard candidates[1] index, prefer same-dtype before arch. Also add explicit seqlen bucket check earlier.
morgan: agree. Also add a perf-ci job that simulates a missing kernel and measures the soft_fallback penalty so we can set FALLBACK_THRESH empirically.
infra-oncall: @alex can you open a hotfix to restore the gfx90a registry entry while we stabilize routing? We can roll that forward then land the bigger autotune change.
alex: will open PR with hotfix + smoke perf test. tagging perf-signal and eng-runtime-oncall.
ci-bot: perf-ci #746 queued by alex. Preliminary run: revert restores throughput to ~2050 tok/s (close to baseline).
priya: nice. follow-up: add telemetry field "kernel_registration_excluded_reason" (enum) so we can see how often arch filters or flags remove entries.
morgan: also add a DEBUG log event "candidate_arch_mismatch" instead of INFO to reduce noise.
alex: filing two issues: AUTOTUNE-216 (seqlen buckets + routing change) and TELE-89 (exclusion reasons + counters). I'll include the perf test cases and a short playbook for canary. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: deploy-bot scheduled canary for rocm-mi250 int8 path tomorrow 09:00 PDT.
alex: ack. I'll watch SLO dashboards and KV hit rates during the canary. Thanks all!
